articles.title: Dylan Larkin, Connor Hellebuyck and the Top NHL Dramas From Summer 2026
articles.summary: The Summer of 2026 could be considered among the most consequential in recent NHL history.
articles.body:
The Summer of 2026 could be considered among the most consequential in recent NHL history.

An "Original Six" team made numerous changes in hopes of returning to playoff-contender status.

Two stars' trade requests become public knowledge, sparking weeks of speculation about their potential destinations. One of them resulted in a team's long search for a new general manager.

Meanwhile, a controversial coach received another opportunity to resume his NHL career. A blockbuster trade reunited two brothers, and an offer sheet had far-reaching consequences for teams attempting to re-sign their best players.

Follow along as we examine these stories in what was a summer of drama for the NHL.

Toronto Maple Leafs Overhaul Their Roster

After nine straight appearances in the Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Toronto Maple Leafs missed the cut last season. It led to the firing of general manager Brad Treliving on March 30 , kicking off an offseason filled with drama in Leafs Nation.

Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment president Keith Pelley drew criticism for his handling of the issues that led to the club's downfall and his plans for the team.

The flak intensified when he hired former Arizona Coyotes general manager John Chayka as the Leafs' new GM. Chayka faced searing questions from the Toronto sports media during his introductory press conference about his tenure with the Coyotes, including the circumstances that led to his firing in 2020.

Despite his critics, Chayka wasted little time making changes in the front office, behind the bench, and within the roster. Among them was replacing Craig Berube as head coach with former Los Angeles Kings bench boss Jim Hiller.

Chayka's roster moves included acquiring starting goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky, first-pairing defenseman Darren Raddysh, and forwards Nick Paul, Jack Roslovic, Colton Sissons, Teddy Blueger, and Brandon Duhaime.

The most notable addition was winger Gavin McKenna. Chosen first overall after the Maple Leafs won the 2026 draft lottery, providing Leafs fans with a ray of hope following a miserable season. NHL Central Scouting ranked the 18-year-old as the top prospect in the 2026 draft class.

On paper, the Maple Leafs seem better than last year's bunch. Whether they'll be good enough to return to playoff contention remains to be seen. Nevertheless, the early offseason turmoil in the league's biggest market drew plenty of attention among NHL followers.

Detroit Red Wings Search For a New General Manager

On July 15, the Detroit Red Wings surprised the hockey world by announcing that Steve Yzerman was no longer their general manager and executive vice president. He'd been GM since 2019 but failed to end a postseason drought that reached a decade by the end of last season.

Yzerman is a franchise icon for leading the Red Wings to three Stanley Cups during his 22-season Hall of Fame playing career. As Tampa Bay Lightning GM, he'd built the foundation of the roster that became Cup champions in 2020 and 2021. However, he couldn't replicate that success as the Wings GM.

Dylan Larkin's trade request , which became public in early June, was the last straw. After 11 seasons with the Red Wings, the last six as team captain, the 30-year-old center apparently grew weary of the constant losing. He'd also clashed with Yzerman .

Two weeks after Yzerman was relieved of his duties, the Red Wings announced they'd hired a search firm to find a suitable replacement. The intention was to find an analytics-driven general manager.

As the calendar flipped to September, however, the Wings haven't found a new GM. With training camp fast approaching and the regular season less than three weeks away, NHL insiders claimed that several potential candidates hadn't even been interviewed yet.

While questions arose about the search process, others wondered if the new general manager would have sufficient time to mend fences with Larkin or find a suitable trade partner among his limited list of trade destinations.

Meanwhile, restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson remains unsigned. He said he'll remain patient and is returning to Detroit for training camp . However, he can't participate unless he's under contract, adding further intrigue to an already puzzling drama.

Mike Babcock Becomes the Edmonton Oilers' New Head Coach

On June 23, the Edmonton Oilers named Mike Babcock as their new head coach , replacing Kris Knoblauch, who had guided them to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025.

Babcock's hiring was rumored for weeks. However, the move still raised eyebrows around the league given his controversial history since 2019.

Before that year, Babcock was considered among the NHL's most respected and successful head coaches. He'd guided the Anaheim Ducks to the Stanley Cup Final in 2003, the Detroit Red Wings to a Stanley Cup championship, and coached Canada to Olympic gold in 2010 and 2014.

Hired by the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2015, Babcock quickly turned their rebuilding roster into a perennial playoff team. However, he was replaced by Sheldon Keefe in November 2019 following a poor start to the season.

Soon after Babcock's firing, he was accused of bullying and mistreating players , going back to his days with the Ducks. Hired by the Columbus Blue Jackets on July 1, 2023, he stepped down before training camp that fall following accusations that he improperly viewed players' smartphones.

Babcock was cleared to return to coaching following a league review. Oilers stars Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and Zach Hyman also endorsed him , with Hyman crediting the embattled coach for helping his development during his tenure with the Maple Leafs.

Nevertheless, Babcock's hiring received mixed reactions on social media. Some believe the Oilers could benefit from being held accountable by an old-school, hard-nosed coach, while others doubt this story will end well. If so, the drama may be just getting started in Edmonton.

Brady Tkachuk Traded to the Florida Panthers

Several notable trades took place during the summer of 2026 . The Washington Capitals acquired wingers Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou. The Chicago Blackhawks brought in Bowen Byram. The San Jose Sharks traded for Darnell Nurse, and the Utah Mammoth traded for Vincent Trocheck.

However, the biggest and most dramatic move occurred on June 21, when the Florida Panthers acquired winger and team captain Brady Tkachuk from the Ottawa Senators in exchange for two first-round picks in the 2026 draft, a second-rounder in 2027, and a conditional first-rounder in 2029.

It had long been rumored that Tkachuk wanted to join the Panthers and play alongside his older brother, Matthew. Brady spent the past two years denying the conjecture , claiming he was fully committed to the Senators and the city of Ottawa.

Senators general manager Steve Staios also denied the rumors . Following the Tkachuk trade, however, he admitted the 26-year-old winger requested a trade 10 days after their season ended on Apr. 25, when the Carolina Hurricanes swept them in the first round of the playoffs.

Tkachuk said he requested the trade to start the next chapter of his career. He thanked the Senators and the city of Ottawa for their support and belief in him, but felt he had a better chance of winning with the Panthers.

Since the trade, the Senators' players have claimed they've put it behind them and are moving on. Staios wasted little time attempting to replace his former captain's scoring, acquiring wingers William Eklund and Andre Burakovsky.

However, the trade left some Senators fans feeling betrayed . That could make for an interesting situation when Tkachuk returns to Ottawa to face his former team on Oct. 21.

Trade Requests by Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck

An NHL player's trade request rarely becomes public knowledge. In most cases, they aren't revealed until after the move takes place, as when the Ottawa Senators shipped Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers on June 21.

However, the summer of 2026 saw two notable stars' trade requests become common knowledge, sparking speculation among fans and pundits about the reasons and the potential destinations.

On June 5, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin had requested a trade. Nearly three months later, on Aug. 27, Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck revealed that he also asked to be traded.

Larkin, 30, has spent his entire 11-season NHL career with the Red Wings, the last five as team captain. He didn't reveal the reason behind his request, but it's believed he's frustrated over the club's decade-long playoff drought and tensions with GM Steve Yzerman, who was relieved of his duties in mid-July.

Hellebuyck is the only active three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also won the Hart Memorial Trophy in 2024-25 and backstopped Team USA to Olympic gold in men's hockey in February. In a statement, he said it was best for him and his family to move on to a team where he could win the Stanley Cup.

Larkin and Hellebuyck are attempting to pressure their respective teams into moving them quickly. Some observers considered their trade requests examples of growing player empowerment as they seek to assert more control over their careers.

However, Larkin remains with the Red Wings as they search for a new general manager, indicating he'll report to their training camp this week. Meanwhile, Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff has a history of patiently waiting for the right deal, which could force Hellebuyck to stick around longer than expected .

On July 3, the Philadelphia Flyers stunned the NHL world by signing Anaheim Ducks restricted free agent center Leo Carlsson to a five-year offer sheet worth a league-record average annual value of $18 million.

Offer sheets were once a rarely used tactic by NHL general managers to try to sign away another team's restricted free agents. Because they're usually matched, they're often considered a waste of time. Another deterrent is the expensive compensation rate owed to the losing team.

In recent years, however, a few teams have had some success . In August 2021, the Carolina Hurricanes signed away center Jesperi Kotkaniemi from the Montreal Canadiens. Three years later, the St. Louis Blues signed winger Dylan Holloway and defenseman Philip Broberg from the Edmonton Oilers.

The Carlsson offer sheet, however, was significant because of how much the promising 21-year-old center received. For several days, fans and reporters mulled over what the Ducks would do before they ended the suspense by matching the offer on July 9 .

It was a bold attempt by the Flyers to address their need for a first-line center. By matching the offer, the Ducks found themselves with limited salary-cap space and a rising star, Cutter Gauthier, to re-sign. To address that issue, they terminated winger Chris Kreider's contract.

The Carlsson offer sheet was possible because of the dramatic increase in the NHL salary cap from $95.5 million to $104 million. It kicked off a rapid rise in salaries for star players regardless of where they are in their respective careers.

Carlsson's league-leading AAV was swiftly replaced by rising star Macklin Celebrini's $18.8 million AAV on a five-year extension with the San Jose Sharks. Colorado Avalanche superstar Cale Makar broke that record a month later with a $20.4 million AAV on an eight-year deal.

It also prompted some teams to avoid future offer-sheet risks by signing their promising youngsters to lucrative deals at previously unheard-of amounts. The most notable example was the eight-year extension worth $9.38 million AAV signed by Vancouver Canucks defenseman Zeev Buium on Sep. 4.

Stats and standings via NHL.com . Salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Maple Leafs GM John Chayka shares latest Auston Matthews extension outlook ahead of new NHL season
articles.summary: NHL News: Toronto Maple Leafs GM John Chayka discusses Auston Matthews’ future with the team, stating there’s no rush for a contract extension as they focus on the upcoming NHL season and team success.
articles.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are heading into the new NHL season with Auston Matthews still under contract for two more years. The captain will make $13.25 million a year for the rest of his deal, buying Toronto some time before he can test the market as a free agent.Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka has admitted the team is eager to keep Matthews beyond his current contract. But it doesn’t sound like an extension is the front office’s priority right now, with the team focused on getting the upcoming campaign up and running first.John Chayka discusses Auston Matthews Toronto Maple Leafs extension The Toronto Maple Leafs have time to get Auston Matthews’ contract situation sorted out, and they are not rushing negotiations, John Chayka says.Matthews could be an unrestricted free agent when his deal ends. That timeline has made his long-term future one of the big storylines around the Toronto franchise, especially since he is the captain and one of the premier goal-scorers in the league.There were about 10 months before the situation became more critical, giving the agency plenty of time to work with Matthews and his representatives, Chayka said.The Maple Leafs seem to be comfortable with where they are with Matthews and his camp. Chayka stressed that discussions can happen when the time is right, rather than being a distraction before the regular season starts.Auston Matthews remains focused on Maple Leafs successMatthews’ priorities also seem to match up well with Toronto’s short-term goals. Chayka said his talks with the captain were about what's best for the organization, not the front office needing to convince him of its direction.That relationship could prove important as Toronto seeks to bounce back from missing the postseason. Matthews has already hit plenty of personal milestones and an Olympic gold medal, but the ultimate unfinished business is to win the Stanley Cup with the Maple Leafs.The larger conversation about Matthews and Toronto could be greatly impacted by the coming season. A big campaign would help show the franchise is headed in the right direction with its captain in the middle.Matthews will also be expected to lead an offence that can get the team back to the playoffs. Of course, the club's overall results, as well as his performance, could influence future conversations about the franchise's long-term direction.For the moment, Chayka's message is simple. The Toronto Maple Leafs want Matthews to stay with the organization, but there is no indication that an extension has to be done immediately. The most important thing is to win games first, and the contract business will be there when the time is right.Toronto Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka has spoken about Auston Matthews’ potential contract extension, saying there is no urgency to hammer out a deal. Matthews has two years remaining on his current deal but is more concerned with team success. The franchise is looking to make a return to the playoffs and hopes to keep hold of their captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Who is Hannah White? Meet ex-college basketball point guard who is branded as ‘real life Barbie’ by fans as she steals the show at US Open 2026
articles.summary: International Sports News: Former college basketball star Hannah White turned heads at the US Open with her glamorous appearance in New York. The 24-year-old shared a series of .
articles.body: Former college basketball star Hannah White turned heads at the US Open with her glamorous appearance in New York. The 24-year-old shared a series of pictures from her day at the tennis Grand Slam, quickly drawing praise from her huge social media following.White looked stunning in a pink tweed dress and sunglasses as she enjoyed the tournament atmosphere. She also posed with the famous Honey Deuce cocktail in her hand. Her outfit became the main talking point, with fans filling the comments with compliments and calling the former Cleveland State star a “real life Barbie”.Who is Hannah White? Basketball star wows fans with Barbie-inspired US Open lookHannah White shared a glamorous montage with her 389,000 Instagram followers after attending the US Open at Flushing Meadows. Several pictures showed her enjoying the tennis action and taking in the atmosphere at the Grand Slam. it was her pink outfit that attracted the most attention.The former Cleveland State University point guard posed in a stylish pink tweed dress. She completed the look with sunglasses and a Honey Deuce cocktail.The outfit quickly caught the attention of her followers. Social media users flooded the comments with compliments after seeing the pictures.One user wrote, “Barbie.” Another added, “This fit so cute.” A third called her a “pretty princess.” Meanwhile, a fourth gushed, “You are everything”, one user wrote, “real-life Barbie”.White’s look fitted perfectly with the colourful atmosphere of the US Open. Her drink also added to the theme.The Honey Deuce is one of the tournament’s most famous traditions. The signature cocktail has been served at the US Open since 2006.The drink is made with Grey Goose vodka, fresh lemonade and raspberry liqueur. It is topped with three honeydew melon balls. The melon pieces are designed to resemble tennis balls.White showed off the drink in several pictures from her visit. She also shared photographs of herself watching matches from inside the venue.The former athlete has built a major social media following since moving on from college basketball. Before becoming known for her online presence, White played point guard for Cleveland State University.Her time on the basketball court gave her a background in competitive sport. However, her social media career now gives fans a different look at her lifestyle.With almost 400,000 Instagram followers, White regularly attracts attention for her fashion and lifestyle posts. Her latest trip to the US Open was no different.The pink dress and glamorous styling has become the focus of her latest post. For White, her latest appearance delivered exactly that. She enjoyed the tennis, posed with one of the event’s signature drinks and gave her followers a glimpse into her day at Flushing Meadows.And judging by the reaction online, the former basketball star certainly made an impression.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Community is how opportunity begins”: How Paige Bueckers’ $50,000 hometown gift grew into a $160,000 lifeline for Minnesota families
articles.summary: International Sports News: Paige Bueckers has become one of basketball’s biggest young stars, but she has not forgotten where her journey began. The Hopkins, Minnesota, native r.
articles.body: Paige Bueckers has become one of basketball’s biggest young stars, but she has not forgotten where her journey began. The Hopkins, Minnesota, native returned the support she received from her hometown in a different way in January 2026. Bueckers offered to match up to $50,000 in donations to the Hopkins Strong Relief Fund, helping families in the community deal with food, rent and other basic needs.For Bueckers, the donation was about more than basketball. She grew up in Hopkins, became a star for the Hopkins Royals and later went on to play at UConn before reaching the WNBA. Even with her career taking her far from Minnesota, she has continued to support the young people and families in the community that helped shape her. Paige Bueckers turned her Hopkins roots into support for familiesOn Jan. 22, 2026, the Hopkins Education Foundation announced that Bueckers would match up to $50,000 in donations to the Hopkins Strong Relief Fund. The foundation had created the fund with ICA Food Shelf to help Hopkins Public Schools students and their families who were struggling with food insecurity and other urgent expenses.The need had grown quickly. Families were dealing with food shortages as well as problems paying rent and utilities, while ICA Food Shelf was receiving more requests for help. The foundation wanted to raise enough money to provide support for families over the next few months.Bueckers decided to step in just days after the relief fund launched. Her offer meant every donation, up to $50,000, could effectively be doubled. The community responded and raised its own $50,000, allowing Bueckers to provide the full match.The Hopkins Education Foundation later said the campaign had raised more than $160,000 in total.Bueckers explained why she wanted to help the place she still considers home. “Community is how opportunity begins. When Hopkins families are supported with food and care, our young people can thrive. That’s why my foundation is committed to supporting the youth and families of Hopkins,” Bueckers said.Her relationship with the community also goes back beyond this particular fundraiser. The Hopkins Education Foundation said Bueckers has supported the ICA Food Shelf’s food market inside Hopkins West Middle School since 2023. The program gives students a way to access food directly at school.That made her latest contribution part of a longer effort rather than a one-time donation.Emily Wallace-Jackson, executive director of the Hopkins Education Foundation, said Bueckers’ support meant a great deal to the community.“Paige’s support means the world to us,” Wallace-Jackson said. “The Hopkins community is so proud of Paige and her accomplishments on the court, but mostly we are proud of her as a person.”The foundation also said that 100% of contributions to the Hopkins Strong Relief Fund would go to ICA Food Shelf. The money was meant to reach children and families in Hopkins Public Schools as quickly as possible. Paige Bueckers $50,000 match helped bring even more support to HopkinsBueckers’ contribution soon became part of a much bigger fundraising effort. The $50,000 match encouraged local residents to donate, and the campaign eventually brought in more than $160,000.The response did not stop there. CBS Minnesota reported in March that Chegg, one of Bueckers’ corporate sponsors, also donated $50,000 to the Hopkins Strong effort.The scale of the need was clear at ICA Food Shelf. Matt Dymoke, the organization’s director of development and communications, said the food shelf had handed out 400 emergency food kits in one week. Before the surge in demand, the organization typically distributed around 90 a month.“She continues to remember us, she continues to remember her neighbors, and it’s just an incredible way for her to give back and for our community to rally around Paige,” Dymoke said.Bueckers’ hometown connection has stayed with her even as her basketball career has moved forward. She went from being a standout at Hopkins High School to becoming a UConn star and then the WNBA Rookie of the Year with the Dallas Wings. Yet her support for the ICA food market shows that she has continued to keep an eye on the community she came from.Her latest donation also gave local families something beyond financial help. It brought more attention to the problems they were facing and encouraged others to contribute. Bueckers put up $50,000, the community matched it, and the effort grew from there.For a player whose career has taken her far beyond Hopkins, the relief fund offered Bueckers a chance to give something back to the people and place that were part of her story long before the WNBA.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Equestrian Anush Agarwalla gives up Asian Games fight; feels 'betrayed' by Federation, IOA, Sports Ministry
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Equestrian Anush Agarwalla conceded his dream of competing in the 2026 Asian Games, which begin on September 19, is over. The rider said he.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Equestrian Anush Agarwalla conceded his dream of competing in the 2026 Asian Games, which begin on September 19, is over. The rider said he felt 'betrayed' after his pleas to the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Sports Ministry and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) went unheard."The dream of Asian Games 2026 is officially over. Words cannot explain the pain and emptiness I feel right now. I have always represented India with immense pride, and always will. But this time, I am deeply hurt - not because I lost, but because I was never given the chance to compete," he wrote in a post."I can accept defeat on the field. That is sport. You fight, you win, you lose, and you come back stronger. But this feels less like defeat and more like betrayal. Accepting an outcome doesn't mean I have to believe the process was right."I fought until the very last moment, and I am proud of that. A fight for a medal is any day a better fight. A fight against the system may never yield a medal, but at least it leaves a record of who stood in the way between me, Floriana, my horse, and the medal we worked for. Maybe I didn't get to fight for the medal. But I made sure the message was registered. Despite reaching out to the Federation, IOA and the Ministry, there was no effort to review what happened. I only hope no athlete has to go through this again. If India wants to become a true sporting nation, athletes deserve a system that is fair, transparent and respects the years of work behind every opportunity," he continued.In July, the Supreme Court had dismissed riders Agarwalla and Sudipti Hajela's pleas challenging the Delhi High Court’s refusal to interfere with their non-selection in the dressage team for the Asian Games.A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe had refused to grant any relief to the two-time Asian Games medallist, saying the court is very reluctant to interfere in individual sports matters.Both riders won gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games and had filed petitions after they were not selected for the upcoming edition by the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI).In August, the Sports Ministry had stressed that it would stick to the selection criterias despite "pressure being created."In its selection criteria unveiled in 2025, the Ministry had made it clear that only those with "realistic chance of winning a medal" would be considered for multi-sport events, including the Asian Games, through selection trials that would be videographed and overseen by independent observers.EFI's ad-hoc committee had first named a selection list in June for the dressage event at the Asian Games, where Agarwalla and Hajela were placed as reserve riders. Agarwalla was named as first reserve and Hajela as second reserve — while four riders were selected ahead of them (Shruti Vora, Gaurav Pundir, Jai Sud and Hriday Chheda).The Asian Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan from September 19 to October 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Westcol confirma la cartelera de Stream Fighters 5: peleas confirmadas y fecha del evento
articles.standfirst: Cartelera oficial de Stream Fighters 5: Valdiri, Blessd y La Divaza al ring
articles.summary: Cartelera oficial de Stream Fighters 5: Valdiri, Blessd y La Divaza al ring
articles.body: El entretenimiento digital y la escena del streaming en Colombia se preparan para uno de los espectáculos más esperados del año. El creador de contenido antioqueño Westcol oficializó la realización de 'Stream Fighters 5', la quinta entrega de la emblemática velada de boxeo de exhibición que reúne a influenciadores, artistas urbanos y personalidades del mundo de internet. El anuncio oficial se transmitió en vivo junto a su equipo de trabajo, donde se revelaron las fechas, la ubicación y las diez peleas que conformarán la programación principal del evento. El evento se llevará a cabo el 14 de noviembre de 2026 en el Coliseo MedPlus de Bogotá. Además del espectáculo deportivo, la velada contará con la presentación musical en vivo del cantante urbano Kris R. Uno de los choques más destacados e inesperados de la noche será el del propio organizador, Westcol, quien se medirá en el cuadrilátero contra el cantante urbano Blessd. Según lo revelado por el streamer, esta pelea contará con una dinámica inédita basada en la incorporación de tecnología con robots. La edición mantendrá enfrentamientos de alto impacto mediático, incluyendo duelos femeninos, un combate multitudinario y peleas entre conocidos creadores de contenido: Con esta quinta edición, Stream Fighters busca consolidarse nuevamente como una de las propuestas de entretenimiento masivo más vistas en la escena digital hispanohablante.

articles.title: ¿Se acaba Win Sports? Dimayor fija fecha decisiva para elegir la nueva canal o señal del fútbol colombiano
articles.standfirst: Definen fecha límite en Dimayor para decidir el futuro de Win Sports y los derechos del FPC
articles.summary: Definen fecha límite en Dimayor para decidir el futuro de Win Sports y los derechos del FPC
articles.body: La incertidumbre sobre el futuro de la transmisión del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano se encuentra en su punto más crítico. La Dimayor citó a una asamblea clave para definir qué empresa o canal de televisión transmitirá los partidos del torneo nacional en las próximas temporadas. El encuentro decisivo se llevará a cabo el próximo lunes 21 de septiembre, fecha en la que los directivos de los clubes afiliados a la Dimayor estudiarán y evaluarán de manera oficial las ofertas económicas recibidas. Tras la deliberación, la asamblea tomará una postura final y comunicará el resultado al canal Win Sports, actual poseedor de los derechos de emisión. El proceso de adjudicación de los derechos de televisión no solo supone un negocio millonario, sino que también ha destapado profundas tensiones en el interior del balompié nacional. Según información revelada por el periodista deportivo Pipe Sierra, existe una marcada división entre el denominado "G8" (los clubes más tradicionales e influyentes del país) y los restantes 28 equipos que integran la asamblea. La disputa gira en torno al manejo de los derechos y a los criterios de distribución de las ganancias que reciben las instituciones por concepto de retransmisión. Esta pugna por los ingresos económicos también se vio salpicada recientemente por el debate público sobre los altos salarios de las grandes figuras de la liga como el reciente de James Rodríguez, evidenciando el ambiente tenso que se vive entre las directivas del balompié local. La asamblea del 21 de septiembre marcará un hito para el ecosistema del fútbol en Colombia. Dependiendo del fallo de las directivas, Win Sports podría renovar y sostener el monopolio de las transmisiones del torneo local, o bien ceder el paso a una nueva propuesta comercial o plataforma. La decisión final no solo dictaminará cómo verán el fútbol los aficionados a partir de los próximos torneos, sino que reorganizará el mapa económico y la repartición de ingresos para los 36 clubes profesionales del país.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard trade grades: Who won the now official Raptors and Clippers deal?
articles.summary: After the Clippers investigation ended, Kawhi Leonard is going back to the Raptors.
articles.body:
FINALLY! After the Los Angeles Clippers investigation over salary cap circumvention ended, there were questions about whether or not Kawhi Leonard would be traded back to the Toronto Raptors , where he won a a championship not too long ago. On Monday? It became official: he's on his way back to the North.

The 35-year-old veteran with $50 million left on his contract was dealt to the Raptors in a trade that didn't change from the first time it was announced back in June. It gives an intriguing Toronto team more juice in a shifting Eastern Conference and gives the Clips some pieces in the future to work with.

So who won this deal? What are the details? As always, we've got you covered. We'll fill you in with who was dealt and hand out some grades to each team:

Clippers get: SF Brandon Ingram , G Gradey Dick , two first-round picks, two second-round picks and one pick swap (more details to come)

The King of the North is back. A team that already has some intriguing pieces -- Scottie Barnes , RJ Barrett , Immanuel Quickley , Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves -- suddenly gets back a future Hall of Famer who proved last year that he can still play. Whether he can play a full season anymore? That's more of the question.

But if you're the Raptors and you feel like you can make some noise in the East by adding a two-way stud like Leonard? You do it. Let's see if they sign him to an extension while they're at it. They didn't give up a ton here for Leonard, so it's a solid deal. And now that the forward is done with the investigation, everyone can rest easy regarding whether or not he'll be suspended (he won't be). GRADE: B+

It feels like the end of an era, one that started with so much promise. Paul George is long gone. Leonard is gone. The Shai Gilgeous-Alexander trade that brought George in the first place was a disaster. The rebuild of sorts has begun. And now the Clips have started getting picks back, which helps after they were hit with some serious penalties in the Leonard investigation.

Yes, trading Leonard and his expiring deal instead of losing him for nothing was somewhat smart. But is Dick good? He's young but last year was not the best. Brandon Ingram was an All-Star, but his contract is enormous.

All in all, this is just a sad moment for the franchise in a stretch of more sadness. Unless Dick develops the way Toronto hoped he would or any of the picks turn out good, it's not the greatest of returns. GRADE: C+

Did anything change in the Clippers and Raptors Kawhi Leonard trade?

No. It's the same as it was when the deal was announced in June.

articles.title: LSU news: Insider drops Kiffin tease for Ole Miss game after viral Clemson rant
articles.summary: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin knows he is the villain. After leaving Ole Miss last season before the playoffs, he allegedly left his dog behind while also tryin...
articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin knows he is the villain. After leaving Ole Miss last season before the playoffs, he allegedly left his dog behind while also trying to bring Ole Miss players to LSU. After all that, he tried to bring in players who were on NFL rosters in the offseason, and LSU ended up being sued. Still, Kiffin started the year with a bag, as LSU routed Clemson 51-10. After the game, a video of Kiffin's halftime speech to the team was leaked .

"Alright guys, we started here like 7-8 months ago, whatever it was. And we asked you to work really hard. And we asked you to come back to work again and again and again. Do you feel good about what happened? Who gives the f**k what happened? That's what's supposed to happen! Ain't no f**king celebrations for that! They're f**king soft! They weren't different! We're f**king different! So you gotta show 'em again!" Kiffin said in the expletive-laden speech before bringing his team out for the second half.

Now, Chris Low of On3 is looking at that speech and the upcoming matchup with Kiffin's former employer, Ole Miss, on Saturday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Kiffin vented to his players in the leaked video, which some have speculated might have been leaked purposely," Low wrote.

It was an intense speech, and it worked out. LSU scored touchdowns on their first two drives of the second half and built a 51-3 lead before Clemson scored on their final drive of the game. Now, that intensity may be coming to Oxford next week.

"You think that was intense? Wait until we get to Oxford," an LSU source told Low.

The game between LSU and Ole Miss is sure to be intense, as it is a clash of two top-ten teams . Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM on Saturday.

articles.title: Casey Woods provides Missouri State football injury update ahead of Marshall game
articles.summary: After suffering a couple injuries against Lindenwood, Missouri State's Casey Woods provides an update entering Week 3 against Marshall.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State secured its first win of the season with a 48-14 drubbing over FCS Lindenwood on Saturday, Sept. 12. In the win, however, the Bears suffered some key injuries.

During head coach Casey Woods' press conference on Monday, Sept. 14, he gave an update on the health of his roster.

Linebacker Dylan Dixson is set to undergo neck surgery and will miss the season. Dixson did not feature against Lindenwood. His injury did not stem from one particular play, according to Woods.

"I hate that for him and it's something that we will have to fight through," Woods said. "Dylan has had kind of a lingering issue. We did some more research on it and felt like this was the time to correct it."

See our best photos from Missouri State football vs Lindenwood in Week 2

Missouri State's starting center and captain Isaiah Villanueva exited the game against Lindenwood in the first half. He was on the sidelines with a boot for the remainder of the game.

Starting kicker Yousef Obeid did not feature against Lindenwood, either. Punter Stewart McDonald took over kicking duties for Obeid.

Wide receiver Makai Cope was scratched late last week. Cope had one target in the Bears ' defeat to Texas A&M.

"We'll see. I would call them questionable," Woods said about all three players. "I would not say full go just yet."

Linebacker Heiko Malone, who was injured during Week 1, remains out for the season.

Missouri State hosts Marshall at 5:30 p.m. on Saturday, Sept. 19.

articles.title: Scouting Report: Elche
articles.summary: Germán Valera is their chance-creation leader, with eight chances (1.68 per 90) from 429 minutes.
articles.body:
After five LaLiga matches, Elche are creating more attacking threat than last season, with npxG created at 1.13 per 90 compared with 0.97 across last season's 38 games. At the other end, they are allowing 1.37 npxG per 90, up from 1.34. They are scoring 1.13 goals and conceding 2.45 per 90, compared with 1.21 and 1.41 respectively last season.

2025-26's leading chance creator was Germán Valera with 42 chances created (1.27 per 90), 11 of them big, and 4.60 xA. He leads again in 2026-27, now on 8 chances (1.68 per 90) from 429 minutes.

The 2026-27 most-used starters include five of the 11 players in the 2025-26 selection. Gonzalo Villar, Fer Niño, Buba Sangaré, Federico Redondo, Facundo Buonanotte and Tete Morente are now in that group. The centre-backs are receiving the ball deeper than last season. They are winning 5.6 second balls per game, down from 6.2.

Their main source of passing threat remains the left flank in the final third, which accounts for 33%, up from 26% last season. Passes from the right flank in the final third contribute 27%, up from 21% last season.

articles.title: Matthäus and Bergomi honoured at San Siro
articles.summary: A special, heartfelt tribute to two unforgettable champions from Inter’s history: ahead of Inter vs. Udinese, Giuseppe Bergomi and Lothar Matthäus were honou...
articles.body:
A special, heartfelt tribute to two unforgettable champions from Inter's history: ahead of Inter vs. Udinese , Giuseppe Bergomi and Lothar Matthäus were honoured by President and CEO Giuseppe Marotta on the pitch at the Meazza in recognition of their extraordinary careers in Nerazzurri colours.

Lo Zio and Lothar were two pillars of the record-breaking Inter side that stormed to the Scudetto in 1988/89. It was the first in a series of memorable triumphs that also included the 1989 Supercoppa Italiana and the first UEFA Cup in the Club's history, secured in 1990/91 following a two-legged final against Roma . That trophy was Inter's first European success since the era of the Grande Inter.

Matthäus scored 53 goals across four seasons with the Club. During his time at Inter, he won the 1990 World Cup with Germany on Italian soil and lifted the Ballon d'Or. A product of the Nerazzurri Academy, Bergomi spent his entire career at Inter, became captain and made 757 appearances, a total bettered only by Javier Zanetti in the Club's history.

It was an emotional and meaningful occasion, with the entire San Siro crowd giving the two Nerazzurri legends a warm and heartfelt ovation.

articles.title: Is Chris Jones Playing Tonight? Latest on Chiefs All-Pro’s Injury Before Broncos Showdown
articles.summary: Chris Jones was a late addition to the Chiefs injury report ahead of Monday night's season opener against the Denver Broncos. The post Is Chris Jones Playing...
articles.body:
Chris Jones was a late addition to the Kansas City Chiefs ' injury report ahead of their season opener against the Denver Broncos , but the All-Pro defensive tackle appears set to play on "Monday Night Football."

Jones is dealing with a calf injury and did not practice Saturday, Sept. 12. However, the Chiefs did not give him a game status designation on their final injury report, suggesting he is expected to be available against Denver.

The update is welcome news for a Chiefs defense that underwent major changes this offseason. Jones, 32, enters his 11th NFL season as Kansas City 's longest-tenured defender and the veteran leader of a defensive line that now includes several new faces.

Chris Jones Expected to Play Despite Calf Injury

Jones' calf issue surfaced late in the week when Kansas City held him out of Saturday's practice.

Despite the missed session, Jones did not receive a questionable, doubtful, or out designation for Monday night's game.

That puts the veteran on track to take his usual place in the middle of Kansas City's defensive front against the Broncos .

If Jones does have to leave the game or play fewer snaps because of the calf issue, the Chiefs have several options behind him. Rookie Peter Woods, Khyiris Tonga and Bryson Eason can provide additional help on the interior.

Jones remains the centerpiece of the group, but the players surrounding him look much different than they did a year ago.

Chris Jones Embraces Veteran Role on New-Look Chiefs Defense

Jones spent much of training camp alongside players significantly younger than him.

The Chiefs selected Woods in the first round and R Mason Thomas in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Woods, 21, and Thomas, 22, quickly gravitated toward Jones as they adjusted to the NFL.

Jones joked about his new status as one of the older players on Kansas City's roster.

"That's a nice way to say you're old," Jones said, via ESPN's Nate Taylor . "I've been in the league going on 11 years, so, I mean, if they paid attention to the Chiefs any bit, then they've probably seen me on the field."

Kansas City also added Tonga in free agency, giving Jones another interior teammate.

The changes were part of a major overhaul of the Chiefs' defensive line following a disappointing 2025 season. Kansas City missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, ending a run of nine consecutive AFC West titles.

Monday night will provide the first regular-season look at the rebuilt unit. Barring a setback with his calf, Jones will be in the middle of it.

The Chiefs and Broncos kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Monday, Sept. 14.

articles.title: Jets Urged to Make Roster Move Amid Concerns Over ‘Fastest Player’
articles.summary: Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets could do themselves a favor by taking some advice about their current roster. The post Jets Urged to Make Roster Move Amid...
articles.body:
The New York Jets got a big win in Week 1, but Aaron Glenn's squad did not emerge unscathed, resulting in calls for a potential roster move amid some early concerns over second-year wide receiver Arian Smith and rookie Omar Cooper Jr.

The worries are for different reasons, but they are certainly connected.

The Jets placed wide receiver Tim Patrick on injured reserve before the win over the Tennessee Titans . They then lost Cooper to an ankle injury during the contest. Smith did not step up.

"May have to add a WR, with Patrick on IR and Cooper's status uncertain," ESPN's Rich Cimini posted on X on September 14 in reaction to head coach Aaron Glenn's update on Monday morning about Cooper and safety Minkah Fitzpatrick 's status ahead of Week 2. "Arian Smith (dropped his only target) too inconsistent for WR4 role."

Glenn told reporters on Monday, "When it comes to the injuries, I'll have more information this afternoon when it comes to that, when we get most of the evaluations back from both of the players–I'm talking about Minka and Coop.

"Again, it's the same; Minkah with a groin and Coop with an ankle."

The Jets selected Smith with the 110th overall pick of the 2025 draft. He finished his rookie season with seven receptions for 52 yards.

"Smith is the fastest player on the field," NFL.com's Lance Zierlein wrote before the 2025 draft, citing the young Jets playmaker's 36.5 YPC on his 10 TDs during his college career. "He lacks play strength to finish catches when contested and his hands are unreliable, which could lead to NFL quarterbacks losing confidence in him. "

Zierlei believed that Smith "could be a tantalizing option for teams looking to take a chance on his speed late in the draft, but his ball skills are unlikely to improve enough for him to become a long-term option."

The most obvious option the Jets could target would be former New York Giants starter Darius Slayton . The Giants cut Slayton last week. However, Slayton has made it clear that he plans to take his time assessing his options.

Brandin Cooks is another veteran option. However, like Slayton, Cooks could wait to see which teams emerge as early contenders before signing.

From a name-recognition standpoint, Tyreek Hill tops the charts, but health is a major concern.

From there the list of free agent options –which includes Super Bowl champions JuJu Smith-Schuster and three-timer Justin Watson –devolves into players who fit specific roles. Some of them are best-suited for special teams.

That could be all the Jets need if they can produce like they did in Week 1 against the Titans. That is particularly true of their reliance on and efficiency in the run game.

Both Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell had 60-plus yards.

Rookie first-round pick and tight end Kenyon Sadiq also flashed with 21 yards on his three receptions. Breece Hall 's receiving ability is always a threat, too. Whatever Glenn and the Jets do, they surely hope Cooper (and Fitzpatrick) return to action in short order.

articles.title: Forward scores phenomenal 9th goal in 6 games, Liverpool have fee agreed to sign him
articles.summary: Liverpool already have a deal in place to sign a forward. He’s just scored his ninth goal in just six games - a phenomenal run of form.Liverpool did a lot of...
articles.body:
Liverpool already have a deal in place to sign a forward. He's just scored his ninth goal in just six games - a phenomenal run of form.

Liverpool did a lot of work moving on homegrown talent under Richard Hughes. They sold virtually all of it, really, as just about every homegrown player near the first-team level was moved on.

Only the injury Conor Bradley remains as a genuinely homegrown player who competes at the first-team level. It's something we imagine they'll come to regret quite badly.

Liverpool are already up against their foreign-player quota, for one. They've also just gutted the culture of the side - something Mohamed Salah called out last season. Having players who have been at the club long-term, even as a youth player, makes a significant difference to establishing methods and standards.

The Reds disregarded that in its entirety. But that doesn't mean they can't get it back.

For one, Liverpool have clauses in place to re-sign some of their sold players. Jarell Quansah is a very obvious one with a pure buyback clause, while someone like Tyler Morton has a percentage of the fee going back to the Reds - essentially a discount.

One very interesting ex-player is Trent Koné-Doherty , who left Liverpool back in January for Molde. The winger was right on the cusp of the first-team level at Anfield, only to struggle for any sort of game time under Arne Slot.

He moved on, heading to Norway in an attempt to play regularly and show what he can do. He's certainly doing just that.

Koné-Doherty now has nine goals in his last six games for Molde. That includes hatttricks on his last two starts for the club and he now sits among the top of the league for passing and shooting metrics.

This could end up being a proper breakout season, then. The Irish forward is following in Erling Haaland 's footsteps a bit with that - the Manchester City star scored 16 times in his final Molde season before joining Red Bull Salzburg.

So this is a situation that Liverpool will watch closely. As mentioned by the Athletic , the Reds have both a sell-on clause and a buyback clause for Koné-Doherty and may decide to bring him back if his form continues.

He only turned 20 this summer, too, which certainly leaves the door open for rapid development. Don't write him off just yet, then - Koné-Doherty could be a homegrown star for the Reds yet.

articles.title: One Detroit Lions Starter May Have Just Lost His Job
articles.summary: Ben Bartch impressed after Christian Mahogany’s Week 1 injury, potentially reopening the Detroit Lions’ competition at starting left guard.
articles.body:
Christian Mahogany won the Detroit Lions ' starting left guard job entering Week 1.

One injury and one solid relief performance later, the competition may already be open again.

Mahogany started Sunday's 31-30 overtime victory over the New Orleans Saints but lasted only 11 offensive snaps before suffering an injury. Veteran Ben Bartch replaced him and played the remaining 66 snaps , giving Detroit an extended look at the player who had been pushing Mahogany for the job right up until the regular-season opener.

That performance has prompted AtoZ Sports to raise the possibility that Bartch may have done enough to take over the position , regardless of how quickly Mahogany is cleared medically.

Detroit wanted a genuine competition at left guard all summer.

In June, Dan Campbell made clear that Mahogany would have to earn the position, something we examined when Campbell confirmed the Lions had a legitimate left guard competition brewing . Bartch was supposed to be one of Mahogany's primary challengers, but injuries prevented Detroit from getting a complete evaluation during training camp.

The Lions were still sorting it out days before Week 1. The team's official site reported that Mahogany and Bartch were splitting first-team repetitions during Saints week before Mahogany ultimately received the start.

Then the game created the extended audition training camp never did.

According to AtoZ Sports, citing Pro Football Focus' initial grading, Bartch finished with a 66.5 overall grade , including a 63.7 run-blocking grade and 67.9 in pass protection. Most importantly, he was credited with allowing zero sacks and zero pressures .

That is a solid afternoon for a player entering cold.

This does not mean Mahogany played his way out of anything.

Quite the opposite. He earned a 76.8 PFF grade in his limited Week 1 action, but 11 snaps are hardly enough to draw sweeping conclusions. His injury, not his performance, opened the door for Bartch.

Initial news on Mahogany was encouraging. Dan Campbell said the first scan came back negative, although Detroit was not ready to declare him out of danger, and the issue may be more hip-related than the knee injury initially announced. Pride of Detroit reported that update after Sunday's game .

The timing matters because Detroit plays Buffalo on Thursday.

Even if Mahogany avoids a significant injury, asking him to turn around four days later may not make sense if Bartch gives the Lions a healthy and reliable alternative.

Detroit already entered Week 1 with offensive-line uncertainty. We noted before the opener that the Lions were taking a calculated risk with their interior depth , particularly with Cade Mays unavailable at center.

Now the short week puts that depth directly into focus.

The interesting question comes after Buffalo.

If Mahogany is unavailable Thursday, Bartch should have another full game to make his case. If he performs well against the Bills, Campbell could face a considerably more difficult choice when Mahogany is ready to return.

Mahogany offers power and upside. Bartch offers experience and, at least Sunday, gave Detroit steady play in both phases.

There is also no reason for the Lions to make a permanent declaration immediately. Detroit could evaluate both players over multiple games or even rotate them if necessary. Campbell has spent months emphasizing competition rather than entitlement along an offensive line that needed improvement after 2025.

That philosophy does not suddenly disappear because Week 1 is over.

Bartch just made sure the competition may not be finished.

articles.title: Steichen with injury update on Colts' Alec Pierce after Week 1 game
articles.summary: Following the Colts' Week 1 matchup with the Ravens, Shane Steichen provided an injury update on WR Alec Pierce.
articles.body:
Coming off the Indianapolis Colts' Week 1 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens , head coach Shane Steichen said that wide receiver Alec Pierce 's left hand/wrist is fine, according to Mike Chappell of FOX59.

Following Sunday's game, Chappell wrote that Pierce briefly exited the game and was taken to the locker room after his left wrist hit the helmet of Ravens' linebacker Roquan Smith at some point in the first half.

Chappell added that Pierce's X-rays came back negative. He then spoke to the Colts ' wideout about the injury after the game.

"It's good,'' Pierce told Chappell . "I just bruised up my hand. No worries.''

Pierce underwent offseason ankle surgery that landed him on the PUP list for much of training camp. He has spent the past few weeks ramping up, which included taking on a smaller role in Sunday's game.

Out of 54 offensive plays, he was on the field for 32 of them, according to PFF.

Pierce finished the game with four receptions for 61 yards . He led the team in receiving.

articles.title: Kris Bubic to Join Dodgers For Reds Series Following Deadline Deal, IL Stint
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Kris Bubic will join the Dodgers at some point during their series against the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Kris Bubic will join the Dodgers at some point during their series against the Cincinnati Reds , per Maddie Lee of The LA Times.

The southpaw likely won't immediately rejoin the team, having made a rehab appearance in Triple-A on Sunday, but will be back before the end of the four-game set.

Bubic arrived from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline in exchange for right-hander Carlos Duran , who had spent the entire season in Triple-A despite holding a 40-man roster spot. Bubic had been on the injured list for the majority of the season, having gone down with an elbow injury in May.

He made nine starts prior to his injury, posting a 4.11 ERA through 50.1 innings with 51 strikeouts. That isn't entirely indicative of his ability, though, as he had a career year just last season. He earned his first All-Star selection in 2025 with a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts.

Duran has two appearances under his belt for the Royals so far, and has allowed two earned runs through 1.1 innings pitched.

What Role Will Kris Bubic Have Upon His Return?

Bubic, despite being a starter for the majority of his MLB career, will likely take on a bullpen role whenever it is he comes off of the injured list.

He came out and expressed his willingness to take on any role after being traded, especially since he played a full season in the bullpen just two years ago.

"I've had experience in pretty much any role possible in the big leagues, a little more recently in a more high-leverage role back in 2024 when we were in the postseason. So I'm open to doing that again," Bubic said.

His move to the bullpen couldn't come at a better time, as the Dodgers struggled through the final two games of their series against the Miami Marlins —though the bigger issue presented itself on Sunday.

The Dodgers held a 4-2 lead heading into the ninth inning, and allowed four runs without recording an out to gift the Marlins a series win. If Bubic takes on a high-leverage role for the team, he could help stabilize a bullpen which doesn't have a clear-cut pitcher for key situations.

articles.title: White Sox's postseason hopes might rely on two breakout pitchers
articles.summary: These two pitchers could be the difference between a postseason run and not.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are 76-73 entering play on Monday, September 14. They're just 0.5 games up on the Cleveland Guardians and fittingly begin a series against their division rivals in Cleveland to get the week started.

If they struggle during this series, not only could the White Sox lose their AL Central lead, but they might even drop out of the postseason field entirely. This is a pivotal series, and the end of the season is still very important to Chicago.

One AL scout told ESPN's Jesse Rogers that the White Sox can be a "sleeper" postseason team if two pitchers can perform at a high level.

White Sox need two key pitchers to play well to have a chance in October

"If the White Sox can get just a little starting pitching, they could still make some noise," an AL scout told Rogers. "They have a bullpen. That's always a need in the playoffs. And they can hit home runs. They just haven't lately. I like them as a sleeper, assuming [Davis] Martin or [Sean] Burke are good."

Whether it's during the postseason or just to get there, Will Venable and the White Sox need Sean Burke and Davis Martin to play well.

The White Sox have a good bullpen and an offense led by Munetaka Murakami and Miguel Vargas that can actually compete with the best of the best around MLB.

But to actually make a postseason run, let alone get there, the White Sox need to get better production from their starting rotation.

While Luis Castillo , Anthony Kay , Erick Fedde and David Sandlin could help the rotation, it's really Burke and Martin who need to perform at a high level to have a chance.

The rest of the rotation is not nearly as important. Having two ace-level pitchers in October is all a team needs to go on a run. Martin and Burke are the White Sox's best chance at getting that this season.

Burke and Martin have to be better than they've been, especially lately, if the White Sox want to make a run this October.

If they continue to struggle, not only would a postseason run seem a bit out of reach, but there's a chance they fail to even make the playoffs with the Guardians and Toronto Blue Jays and Texas Rangers hot on their tail.
